clue.text: Showed touching affection

parts.note: touching reads as both moving and physically in contact, so the fond gesture is a stroke of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: To stroke someone fondly is literally to show affection by touch.

clue.text: Looks closely-about time to be wearing glasses

parts.note: someone wearing a coat is in it

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the glasses word is placed around the time letter

parts.note: specs is the everyday short word for spectacles

explanation.surface: Someone peers intently, saying it is high time they put their spectacles on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' gives IN because a worn coat is one you are in; 'to be' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise or examine something is to look at it closely.

clue.text: Overburden journalists with work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the press is the collective name for reporters

explanation.surface: Reporters are being swamped with too many assignments.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh down people harshly with heavy burdens is to tyrannise them.

clue.text: A binding affair is arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters of the word before it are reordered

explanation.surface: A deal that legally ties the parties together is being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A binding' looks like an adjective on 'affair'; it is the definition, a material used to bind things.
explanation.definitionFit: This palm fibre is used as tying material by gardeners and craftworkers.

clue.text: Roughly appropriate greeting to sailor

parts.note: hi is a casual hello
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a seaman is about the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly appropriate' reads as 'more or less suitable', but it means seize by force, with 'appropriate' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer a vehicle by force is to take it over violently.

clue.text: Good diction, perhaps, but it can cause offence

definitions.meaning: blunt, frank talk can upset people

explanation.surface: Clear pronunciation is admirable, yet it may still upset people.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear enunciation is speaking plainly in sound, while blunt candour is speaking plainly in meaning and can hurt.

clue.text: Ne who breaks down the constituents of a Hitchcock film

definitions.text: Ne who breaks down the constituents of a Hitchcock film

parts.words: Ne who breaks down the constituents of a Hitchcock film
parts.note: a person analysing the parts of the 1960 Hitchcock thriller titled for a disturbed mind, or of the mind itself

explanation.surface: A film critic dissects the elements of a famous Hitchcock movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hitchcock film is Psycho; one who analyses the psyche is a therapist of the Freudian kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist of the Freudian school analyses the mind into its hidden elements.

clue.text: Soldier-husbands who try to supply everything

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
to husband resources is to save or stock them, as stores does

explanation.surface: Army men who are married try hard to provide for every need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husbands' is a verb here, meaning saves up; village shops of this kind sell a bit of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Village shops of this kind sell a wide range of goods, aiming to stock whatever is needed.

clue.text: Stimulate with increased intensive publicity

parts.note: hype is aggressive promotion
prices that are up have increased

explanation.surface: A promotion campaign is ramped up to excite the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or energise someone is to work them into a heightened state.

clue.text: Stops in bars

definitions.meaning: desists or holds back, as a verb
repeated passages of a song, choruses

explanation.surface: A drinker stays away from pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but it means passages of music; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back means desisting; choruses repeated in songs are the recurring musical lines.

clue.text: Wee startled animal

indicators.note: startled means jolted, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tiny creature is frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a farm animal.

clue.text: In radiography sickness has a cure

indicators.note: in means the letters are found sitting inside the words radiography sickness

explanation.surface: An X-ray department finds that radiation sickness can be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for medicine or a remedy, as in the phrase heal thyself.

clue.text: Streaks wildly round mid-afternoon-like this?

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters are wrapped around another letter
wildly means without order, so the letters of streaks are scrambled
mid means the central letter of afternoon is taken

explanation.surface: Someone runs naked across a field in the middle of the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' scrambles STREAKS; 'round' puts it around R, the middle letter of 'afternoon'; a streaker is naked, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Streakers run naked, and this British slang word means completely nude.

clue.text: Regret being a bitter-scented shrub

definitions.meaning: an aromatic herb with bitter leaves

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to be a sharp-smelling bush.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sorry for something is to lament it; the herb of grace is an aromatic evergreen plant.

clue.text: His fancies rarely last

parts.note: a person whose enthusiasms are short-lived, always taking up the latest craze

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows passing crazes keeps switching enthusiasms.

clue.text: It is charged for a portion without wine

indicators.note: without means the wine word is taken away from the letters of portion

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A fee is charged for a serving that comes with no wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests paying, but it means carrying electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule carrying an electric charge is this particle.

clue.text: They work against the grain

parts.note: the idiom for being contrary, read literally as pests that eat stored cereal

explanation.definitionFit: These beetles infest and destroy stored cereal crops.

clue.text: Organise venue at Leatherhead in future

indicators.note: to organise is to put into order, so the letters of venue at are rearranged

parts.note: the word splits as leather plus head, the head of leather being its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone plans to book a venue in the Surrey town of Leatherhead some time later.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, but the setter reads it as 'head of Leather', its first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will happen at a later time is still to come.

clue.text: Evil once released may lead to brute force

indicators.note: released means set loose, so the letters of evil once are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: Once wickedness is let loose it can end in savagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence is the use of physical force to hurt or damage.

clue.text: It's played when pupils are not in form

definitions.text: It's played when pupils are not in form

parts.words: It's played when pupils are not in form
parts.note: the idiom playing hooky, with form meaning a school class rather than fitness

explanation.definitionFit: Pupils who skip school and miss their class are said to play the truant.

clue.text: Mother to hang about and waste a doctor's time

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
to linger is to loiter

explanation.surface: Mum waits around and wastes the GP's time.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign illness to avoid work is to waste medical attention on a faked complaint.

clue.text: Kind of tank that's brought out for new recruits

indicators.note: brought out suggests letters drawn out into a new arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: IE is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A model of tank is wheeled out for the fresh soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' is a link; 'brought out' rearranges TANK with IE, short for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch of people enrolled at the same time, as in an army or school, is the year's admission.

clue.text: Go to the bullfight arena and witness a bloody spectacle

parts.note: a bullring is the circular arena for bullfights

explanation.surface: A spectator visits a bullfight and sees a gory show.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull piercing someone with its horns is a gory sight.

clue.text: Torpedo carriers ordered to base

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters of to base are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ships with torpedoes are commanded back to port.
explanation.definitionFit: German motor torpedo boats of the Second World War carried these weapons.

clue.text: Badly run vessel

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of run go awry and are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ship is poorly managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall container, for tea or ashes, is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Say their disposition is for emotional instability

indicators.note: disposition, read as arrangement, signals that the letters of say their are rearranged

explanation.surface: People claim their temperament makes them emotionally volatile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled emotional excess is a state of frenzy.

clue.text: They hold an alternative view of things

indicators.note: hold means the letters of they contain another piece

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Some people hold a different opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or set of ideas is one way of explaining the world.

clue.text: Don't seize opportunities to be safely conscious?

definitions.meaning: decline to grab chances, read literally

explanation.surface: Cautious people pass up openings to stay safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing safe means avoiding risks; read literally, the phrase says refusing openings offered.
